notes: Your pages load faster for everyone who is only reading them. The part that keeps your file's own formatting when you save needs an HTML parser, and that parser was a third of everything a visitor had to download before your page appeared. It now waits until you sign in to edit, so a reader never downloads it at all and the rest arrives sooner.

Nothing about saving changes. When you edit, it is fetched in the background while you work, and your save keeps your formatting exactly as before. On the rare occasion it cannot be reached, the page still saves; it just rewrites the formatting, which is what it did before this feature existed.

When you ask AI for a new page, the page now starts with your own words. The AI sometimes wrote a sentence introducing itself at the top, left a stray line of punctuation behind it, and pushed the page's title out of place; all of that is gone.

On a page AI built for you, the facts in a table or a list can be changed. Opening hours, prices, a list of what to bring: these are now editable on the page and they appear in the content form, where before they were the one thing you could never correct.
A long answer from AI is no longer cut off. Pages that take a few minutes to write now finish, and an AI that has genuinely stopped replying is reported sooner, in a sentence that says what happened.
Keeping an AI edit no longer leaves an invisible mark in your saved file. It was harmless to read, but it built up with every edit and made the file look changed when it was not.
The publisher no longer tells the AI service who you are. It sends the description you wrote and the template you picked, and nothing else.

The publisher now speaks Spanish, Slovak and Czech the whole way through. The messages it shows while your site goes out, and the warning that a page already exists where you are publishing, used to appear in English whatever language you had chosen.
AI says it has no credit before you write anything, rather than after you have described the page you wanted and waited for it.
The counter moves while AI is thinking. Some models spend the first minute working out what to write before writing a word, and a counter sitting at zero for that long looked broken.
When AI offers to change something, you see what is on the page now next to what would replace it. Deciding whether the new wording is better should not be a memory test.

You can now ask AI for a page. In the publisher, open the AI section, describe what you want and look at the result before anything is published; you can start from nothing or from a template. AI runs through our own Routstr node by default and is paid with Cashu or Lightning, and its settings let you choose another node or model, or your own API key.

On a page you already have, click the words or the block you want changed and choose Edit with AI. The result appears as a preview and nothing changes until you keep it. Undo takes an accepted change back, and Save publishes it.

Undo and Redo now sit on the editing bar, so a block you deleted by mistake comes back with its buttons still working. The history lasts for the editing session; your published versions stay in History as before.
Choosing a picture has a crop step now. Pick free, square, wide or 4:3 before the file is uploaded, and only the crop you accept is stored.

The content form learns new field types from the page itself: a date picker, a dropdown, a number field, and a field where you can write with links, lists and bold text. A page that has not been told about them looks exactly as it did.

Saving keeps more of your file as you wrote it. A small change no longer rewrites the punctuation and spacing of the whole document when it does not have to, so the file stays recognisable in a text editor. When that cannot be done safely, the save falls back to exactly what it did before.

The things a page repeats, the events in a list or the cards in a row, can carry the same small strip of buttons the page's blocks already carry: move it, copy it, delete it, in one place with one meaning rather than a different row of words for each kind of thing. It comes with the stylesheet, so a page built from one of the newer templates has it and needs nothing set up. Nothing on a page already published changes, because the buttons it was built with are its own markup and no update rewrites those.

The list of what changed in an update is readable now. Every line arrived cut off mid-word with a sideways scrollbar under it, so the one thing this dialog exists to show you was the one thing you could not read.

Taking an update no longer reloads the page out from under you. It says the newer version is on your site and leaves the reload to you, so you stay signed in and whatever else was on the screen stays there.

A page you have already updated stops asking you to update it again. For a few minutes after you publish, a gateway can still hand out the copy of your page it had before, and that older copy would offer you the same update a second time. It now says the update is published and offers you a reload.
Updating no longer answers you with a list of dead links. Those are about your own pages, they were there before you pressed Update, and you will hear about them the next time you save.

The toolbar speaks the language of the page. On a Slovak, Czech or Spanish page, Write, Edit content, Settings, History and Save stayed in English beside the words that had been translated. A button you renamed yourself is left as you wrote it.

The sign-in box, the settings, the version list and this update offer come out as boxes again on a page whose own stylesheet has a rule about forms. On one site this dialog arrived as four narrow columns with its buttons pushed off the side of the screen, which made it almost impossible to read and nearly impossible to press. The content panel had the same problem on a page that styles its asides.
The box you paste a key into is now as wide as the dialog around it, rather than the small default the browser picks.

A link to a page that is not in your site no longer stops you saving. The page is published, and a panel lists the addresses that lead nowhere and stays on the screen until you close it, with a button that copies the list. Until now one link to a page that did not exist yet meant nothing could be saved at all.
A link written as /shop/ is understood to mean the page at /shop/index.html, the way any web address works, so a site with more than one page stops reporting its own links as broken.

When a save fails, the reason stays on the screen until you dismiss it and can be selected and copied. It used to vanish after two seconds, which is not long enough to read a list of file names, let alone send one to whoever can fix it.
A page that carries no content form no longer shows an Edit content button that opens nothing.
Pasting into a one-line region no longer splits it. A pasted paragraph used to nest a second <a> inside a button, which came back after the next load as two buttons with the first one empty.
A block's rail can reach inside the block. The new ⌷ button lists what a block is made of, so a stray element can be removed without deleting the block around it.
A button's link can be changed. Pressing the link button inside one used to try to put a link inside a link.
Settings says which runtime the page is running, and can move it to a newer one.
A dialog opened on top of another no longer shares its Escape key with the one underneath.

A publish that stalls now ends and says which Blossom server stopped answering, instead of sitting on "Uploading… 1/4" forever. Every network call has a timeout, and each server gets its own line with a running clock.
A blob is signed once rather than once per base64 encoding, which halves how many times a phone signer asks you to approve the same upload.
The publisher has a panel for the relays and Blossom servers it uses, so one server refusing you is something you can work around without a terminal.

A publish asks the Blossom servers what they already hold before it signs anything, so a phone signer is asked once per file rather than once per file per server, all in one burst at the start. Republishing an unchanged site now needs no upload approvals at all.
nc:watch-dom, off by default, makes any change to the page count as an edit rather than only typing.
